about: Plan parity (ADR 0018, ported to release/v0.1.1): one logical input set per case for the Griffin vehicle-side run. src-tauri/tests/plan_parity.rs renders the app's job script into app/<case>.sbatch; tests/test_plan_parity.py renders `coperceive model run --slurm` for the same inputs and compares the two whole scripts line by line against allowed_differences.json. Paths are logical: the CLI builds them under a temporary directory and maps it back. Each case's `python` is the interpreter that runs `model run` (the CLI's --slurm-python, and the interpreter both sides record environment.json with). Each case's `pyvenv_cfg` is the pyvenv.cfg of the venv that holds `python`, on this cluster's /software/python/<version> base: the CLI reads it locally (slurm.py interpreter_module), the app over the plan's read-only interpreter check, and both load that python module after module purge. Each case's `coperceive_root` and `samples` are what the run's python reports on the cluster (the app's read-only plan-python check): the root of the coperceive it imports (the job's PYTHONPATH; the CLI exports the root of the checkout that emitted the job, mapped to code_root) and the pose times of the fixture's 10 scenes x 149 poses, which the CLI counts locally for its --time estimate. A case may also give its own `code_root` (the manifest's folder and PYTHONPATH; the CLI copies the plugin there), `extras` (the model's options: the app's extras, the CLI's --option k=v) and `media_root: false` (no media root). A profile's `proxy_jump` and `port` are the SSH settings the app reaches the cluster with; plan_parity.rs checks they reach the SSH arguments and leave the script byte-identical. `refusals` are inputs the app refuses: plan_parity.rs holds the app to the exact `refused` message (`<stage>: <message>`) and tests/test_plan_parity.py checks that `model run --slurm` takes the same input; `why` and `cite` say why the difference stays.

cases.name: base
cases.about: The release doc's Griffin vehicle run (docs/release/v0.1.1-eval-pipeline-test.md): the scenes folder, an A40 partition that discovery found, the CUDA modules on the profile.

cases.name: mixed_partition
cases.about: A mixed partition whose discovery lists a100 before a40: the app must write --gres=gpu:1 as plan_sbatch does and let the manifest's --constraint="a40" pick the type (a typed gpu:a100:1 beside it would fit no node).

cases.name: modules_no_gpu_discovery
cases.about: A modules profile (python/3.12) on a partition with no GPU discovery: the app must still request a GPU and load the manifest's CUDA modules, as plan_sbatch does.

cases.name: modules_profile_other_python
cases.about: A modules profile that lists its own python/3.11 while the venv that runs coperceive is on /software/python/3.9.18: the app loads only the interpreter's python/3.9.18 (another python module would swap it under Lmod), as plan_sbatch does, and says so in a comment.

cases.name: venv_profile
cases.about: A venv profile (no modules of its own) running `<venv>/bin/python -m coperceive`: the app must still write module purge and the manifest's CUDA modules, as plan_sbatch does for any interpreter.

cases.name: venv_script_command
cases.about: A discovered venv profile whose coperceive command is the console script <venv>/bin/coperceive (server_profiles.rs): the run is that script, environment.json is recorded with <venv>/bin/python, the interpreter pip names in the script's shebang, which is the CLI's --slurm-python.

cases.name: proxy_jump_modules
cases.about: A modules profile (python/3.12, no GPU discovery, a CPU partition) reached through a jump host on port 2222, its data and results under /data, with a model option (min_score=0.05): ProxyJump reaches only the SSH arguments, and the option reaches both `model run` lines alike.

cases.name: spaces_and_quotes
cases.about: Every data path (scenes, raw root, media root) is under a folder with a space, a single quote and double quotes, and the code root (manifest and PYTHONPATH) has a space and a single quote. The results root has none: #170 refuses a results folder with a space, a '#' or a quote (it goes into #SBATCH --output/--error), see the refusal results_root_with_space; a code folder may not hold a double quote (#170).

refusals.name: no_media_root
refusals.about: The base case with no media root, as `model run` allows (--media-root is optional).
refusals.refused: build_run_plan: Choose the media root on the cluster before checking the plan.
refusals.why: The app's built-in model form requires a media root (run_plan.rs build_run_plan, since 9b4d9a0); `model run` treats --media-root as optional, and Griffin finds its camera images through it. ADR 0021 covers the job script for inputs both sides accept and does not decide whether the app should accept an empty media root: an open question for the PM (ADR 0018, "Not decided here"). Pinned so a change either way is seen.

refusals.name: results_root_with_space
refusals.about: The base case with a results root that holds a space (/home/te st/results).
refusals.refused: build_run_plan: The results folder "/home/te st/results" contains a space. Slurm reads this folder from the job script's #SBATCH --output and --error lines, which it splits at spaces and cuts at '#', so the path may not contain spaces, '#' or quotes. Choose a folder whose path has none of these, for example /data/my_lab/runs.
refusals.why: #170: the app writes the results folder into #SBATCH --output/--error, which Slurm splits at spaces and cuts at '#', so a shared profile could add Slurm options to every job. The CLI writes no results folder into an #SBATCH line (its log folder, --slurm-logs, is refused with a space for the same reason: test_model_slurm.py), so it takes this results root.
refusals.cite: CHANGELOG.md Unreleased/Security (results folder); src-tauri/src/hpc.rs validate_sbatch_path; coperceive/models/slurm.py validate_logs_dir
